name: css-image-stacking
title: CSS Image Stacking
description: A dark page of architectural photographs that pin in place as you scroll, each new picture settling over the previous one at a slightly larger width until six images have gathered into a stack.
use: A photography page wants big images to gather into a stack as the reader scrolls.
avoid: Six screens of scroll carry six pictures, all with empty alt text and fixed percentage widths.
a11y: Every photo has empty alt text, so the stack conveys nothing to screen readers, and smooth scrolling ignores reduced-motion. (keyboard: n-a, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Full-height photos of buildings, centred on a near-black page with rounded corners, growing from about half the width to four fifths. Earlier pictures stay pinned behind the newest one with a thin dark gap along the top.
behaves: Scrolling pins each photo section at the top of the viewport so the next picture glides up over it while being a little wider. The pile builds with every section and then the last photo leaves with the page.
customise: No props: the six photo links and their width classes are written section by section in the file, and the heading and footer copy are fixed too.
weight: moderate: Six large remote photos load up front; the stacking itself is plain CSS sticky.
